# PCBA Modification Guide — edge_sensor / asic

**Generated:** 2026-04-12T05:24:58Z
**Target:** ASIC reference board (chipignite_caravel_qfn64)
**KiCad version:** kicad8

This guide tells you exactly what to modify in the upstream template to produce
the edge_sensor asic reference board. Follow these steps
in KiCad 8.x with the template files from `template/`.

## 2. Components to add or modify

The following table maps every component in the edge_sensor spec to a
real KiCad 8 stock symbol + footprint. Components already present in the
template are marked; new ones need to be added.

| Ref | Role | Spec part | KiCad symbol | KiCad footprint | Action |
| --- | ---- | --------- | ------------ | --------------- | ------ |
| U1 | soc | caravel_qfn64 | `TinyTapeout:Caravel_QFN` | `Package_DFN_QFN:QFN-64-1EP_9x9mm_P0.5mm_EP7.65x7.65mm` | **In template** (Caravel QFN-64) |
| U2 | usb_bridge | ft232h | `Interface_USB:FT232H` | `Package_QFP:LQFP-48_7x7mm_P0.5mm` | **ADD** |
| U3 | flash | w25q32jvssiq | `Memory_Flash:W25Q32JVSS` | `Package_SO:SOIC-8_5.23x5.23mm_P1.27mm` | **ADD** |
| U4 | ldo | ap7361_18 | `Regulator_Linear:AP7361C-10E` | `Package_TO_SOT_SMD:SOT-223-3_TabPin2` | **ADD** |
| U5 | ldo | ap7361_33 | `Regulator_Linear:AP7361C-10E` | `Package_TO_SOT_SMD:SOT-223-3_TabPin2` | **ADD** |
| U6 | reset_supervisor | mcp809_300 | `Power_Supervisor:MCP101-270D` | `Package_TO_SOT_SMD:SOT-23` | **ADD** |
| J1 | usb_connector | usb_c_receptacle | `Connector:USB_C_Receptacle` | `Connector_USB:USB_C_Receptacle_HRO_TYPE-C-31-M-12` | **In template** (USB-C) |
| J2 | header | pmod_2x6_female | `Connector_Generic:Conn_02x06_Odd_Even` | `Connector_PinSocket_2.54mm:PinSocket_2x06_P2.54mm_Vertical` | **ADD** |
| J3 | header | tag_connect_10pin | `Connector_Generic:Conn_02x05_Odd_Even` | `Connector_PinHeader_2.54mm:PinHeader_2x05_P2.54mm_Vertical` | **ADD** |
| SW1 | button | reset_button_smd | `Switch:SW_SPST` | `Button_Switch_SMD:SW_SPST_B3U-1000P` | **In template** (reset) |
| D1 | led | led_green_0603 | `Device:LED` | `LED_SMD:LED_0603_1608Metric` | **In template** (LED) |

> **U1** note: Uses the TinyTapeout Caravel_QFN symbol from the template fork submodule. Pin names use mprj_io[N] convention where N is the physical Caravel io index (user GPIO 0 = mprj_io[5]).
> **U4** (`ap7361_18`): set the Value property to `AP7361C-18E (1.8V)` — the stock symbol is a generic variant; the value override selects the correct output voltage / threshold.
> **U4** note: Pin-compatible with all AP7361C-xxE variants; override value to the target voltage
> **U5** (`ap7361_33`): set the Value property to `AP7361C-33E (3.3V)` — the stock symbol is a generic variant; the value override selects the correct output voltage / threshold.
> **U6** (`mcp809_300`): set the Value property to `MCP809-300 (reset supervisor)` — the stock symbol is a generic variant; the value override selects the correct output voltage / threshold.
> **U6** note: MCP809 not in KiCad 8 stock; MCP101 is pin-compatible SOT-23 reset supervisor

## 3. Net connections (signal wiring)

For each net below, draw a wire in the schematic connecting the two endpoints.
Endpoint references use the KiCad pin names from the symbols above. Where the
spec uses `soc.gpio[N]`, the corresponding Caravel I/O pad on the QFN-64 symbol
is listed.

### Pin translation (soc.gpio[N] → Caravel io_in[])

The package `caravel_qfn64` has `user_gpio_offset = 5`, so:

| Spec endpoint | Caravel io index | Signal | Direction |
| ------------- | ---------------- | ------ | --------- |
| `soc.gpio[0]` | `io_in[5]` / `io_out[5]` | uart_rx | input |
| `soc.gpio[1]` | `io_in[6]` / `io_out[6]` | uart_tx | output |
| `soc.gpio[2]` | `io_in[7]` / `io_out[7]` | spi_sclk | output |
| `soc.gpio[3]` | `io_in[8]` / `io_out[8]` | spi_cs_n | output |
| `soc.gpio[4]` | `io_in[9]` / `io_out[9]` | spi_mosi | output |
| `soc.gpio[5]` | `io_in[10]` / `io_out[10]` | spi_miso | input |
| `soc.gpio[6]` | `io_in[11]` / `io_out[11]` | fft_done | output |

### Signal nets

| Net name | From | → | To | Class | Description |
| -------- | ---- | - | -- | ----- | ----------- |
| SOC_GPIO_0__U2_AD1 | `soc.gpio[0]` | → | `U2.AD1` | default | uart_rx ← USB bridge TX |
| SOC_GPIO_1__U2_AD0 | `soc.gpio[1]` | → | `U2.AD0` | default | uart_tx → USB bridge RX |
| SOC_GPIO_2__J2_4 | `soc.gpio[2]` | → | `J2.4` | high_speed | spi_sclk → ADXL355 SCLK |
| SOC_GPIO_3__J2_1 | `soc.gpio[3]` | → | `J2.1` | high_speed | spi_cs_n → ADXL355 CS |
| SOC_GPIO_4__J2_2 | `soc.gpio[4]` | → | `J2.2` | high_speed | spi_mosi → ADXL355 MOSI |
| SOC_GPIO_5__J2_3 | `soc.gpio[5]` | → | `J2.3` | high_speed | spi_miso ← ADXL355 MISO |
| SOC_GPIO_6__TP1_1 | `soc.gpio[6]` | → | `TP1.1` | default | fft_done debug probe |
| SOC_RESET_N__U6_VOUT | `soc.reset_n` | → | `U6.VOUT` | default | POR supervisor drives reset_n |
| U6_VOUT__SW1_1 | `U6.VOUT` | → | `SW1.1` | default | Manual reset button shorts reset_n to GND |
| U3_1__U1_FLASH_CSB | `U3.1` | → | `U1.flash_csb` | default |  |
| U3_2__U1_FLASH_IO1 | `U3.2` | → | `U1.flash_io1` | default |  |
| U3_5__U1_FLASH_IO0 | `U3.5` | → | `U1.flash_io0` | default |  |
| U3_6__U1_FLASH_CLK | `U3.6` | → | `U1.flash_clk` | default |  |

### How to wire in KiCad

1. Open the template schematic in KiCad 8
2. For each **ADD** component in the table above, place the symbol: **Place → Add Symbol** (`A` key), search for the symbol name
3. Assign the footprint: right-click → **Properties** → Footprint field → browse to the footprint listed
4. For each net in the signal nets table:
   - Locate both endpoints on the schematic sheet
   - Draw a wire (`W` key) between them, or use **global labels** if pins are on different sheets
   - For `soc.gpio[N]` endpoints: connect to pin `io_in[N+5]` on the Caravel symbol
5. Run **Inspect → Electrical Rules Checker** and resolve any errors

## 4. Power tree wiring

### VIN (5.0V)

- **Source:** J1.VBUS
- **Loads:**
  - `U4.VIN`
  - `U5.VIN`
  - `U6.VIN`
- **Decoupling per load:** 100nF bypass × 1, 10uF bulk at regulator output
### VCCD1 (1.8V, ±5%)

- **Source:** U4 (budget: 100mA)
- **Loads:**
  - `soc.power.vccd1`
  - `soc.power.vccd2`
- **Decoupling per load:** 100nF bypass × 2, 10uF bulk at regulator output
### VDDA1 (3.3V, ±5%)

- **Source:** U5 (budget: 200mA)
- **Loads:**
  - `soc.power.vdda1`
  - `soc.power.vdda2`
  - `U2.VCC`
  - `U3.VCC`
  - `J2.VCC`
- **Decoupling per load:** 100nF bypass × 1, 10uF bulk at regulator output

### How to wire power

1. Place power symbols (`VCC`, `GND`, or custom power flags) on each power pin
2. Use KiCad's **Power flag** (`PWR_FLAG`) on at least one point per net to
   suppress "power not driven" ERC warnings
3. Add decoupling capacitors near each load pin (right-click → place `Device:C`
   with the specified value + an 0603/0805 footprint)

## 5. After schematic changes — update the PCB

1. **Save the schematic** (`Ctrl+S`)
2. **Open the PCB editor** (`F8` from the schematic, or open `*.kicad_pcb` directly)
3. **Tools → Update PCB from Schematic** (`F8` in pcbnew) — this creates footprints
   for newly-added components and creates rats-nest (airwire) connections for new nets
4. **Place new footprints** — drag them to sensible positions near the Caravel QFN-64:
   - FT232H near the USB-C receptacle
   - QSPI flash near the SoC (short traces for signal integrity)
   - LDOs near the board edge (thermal dissipation via copper pour)
   - ADXL355 Pmod header on the board edge (accessible for cable)
5. **Route traces** — either manually (`X` key) or via **Tools → FreeRouting** plugin
   for automatic routing of the newly-added nets. The template's existing routing
   (Caravel power/flash/clock) is preserved.
6. **Run DRC** — **Inspect → Design Rules Checker** → confirm no new violations
   introduced by the modifications. Baseline violations (from the template) are
   documented above.

## 6. Export deliverables

After DRC passes, export the contest deliverables:

```bash
# From the Ubuntu box (KiCad 8 installed):
kicad-cli sch erc     <stem>.kicad_sch -o reports/erc.json --format json
kicad-cli pcb drc     <stem>.kicad_pcb -o reports/drc.json --format json
kicad-cli pcb export gerbers <stem>.kicad_pcb -o gerbers/
kicad-cli pcb export drill   <stem>.kicad_pcb -o gerbers/
kicad-cli pcb export step    <stem>.kicad_pcb -o <stem>.step
kicad-cli pcb export svg     <stem>.kicad_pcb -o inspection/<stem>.svg \
    --layers "F.Cu,B.Cu,F.SilkS,Edge.Cuts"
kicad-cli sch export pdf     <stem>.kicad_sch -o inspection/<stem>_schematic.pdf
```

Or use the automated runner:
```bash
bash scripts/pcba_phase3b_ubuntu.sh
```

## 7. BOM cross-reference

The generated BOM at `bom/edge_sensor_asic_bom.csv` is
the authoritative parts list. After completing the schematic modifications,
verify the KiCad-exported BOM matches:

```bash
kicad-cli sch export bom <stem>.kicad_sch -o bom/<stem>_bom_kicad.csv
diff bom/edge_sensor_asic_bom.csv bom/<stem>_bom_kicad.csv
```

Any differences indicate a component was added in the schematic but not in the
spec (or vice versa). Reconcile before committing to the contest repo.
